rows.why_long: Hard Rock under 4.5 at -111 needs 53% to pay; fair after the vig 50%. Averaging 24.0 over the last 8 games, lower than 4.5 in 26% of them (raw 17%, shrunk 43%). WAS allows +4% to TEs → projects 22.6 (raw 19%, shrunk 42%).
why_points: The bet: Rec yds under 4.5 at -111. To make money it has to win 53% of the time. The betting market, with the sportsbook's cut removed, gives it 50%.
Game log, most recent first: 35, 11, 0, 9, 0, 72, 29, 77. Weighted average 24.0; went lower than 4.5 in 2 of 8 games (26% recency-weighted).
Trending down: last 3 games average 15.3 vs 37.4 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±24.8, so the line is 0.8 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a meaningful gap.
Market: ESPN Bet make this side 48% once their cut is removed; Hard Rock's price needs 53%. Hard Rock charges more than the market for this side.
Matchup: WAS has allowed +4% vs the league average to TEs (already shrunk toward average for sample size).
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): +7% on his average.
PFF: WAS plays man on 21% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 25%); he gains 1.28 yds/route vs man and 1.38 vs zone → +0% from scheme.
PFF: WAS allows 1.53 yds/route to TEs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.45) → +7% against his usual opponents.
PFF: He lines up in the slot 54% of the time; WAS's slot defenders allow 1.49 yds per coverage snap (league 1.59, tighter).
Projection: we expect 22.6 receiving yards on average; in a typical game 16.5 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 12.0 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 17% and the matchup 19%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 43%, matchup 42%.
Bottom line: we give it 42% to win and it needs 53%. The edge is the difference: -10.2 points; that works out to about -19¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
rows.glance_head: Pass: we expect about 16.5 in a typical game vs the 4.5 line — if anything the other side.
